Where it began

Rehan Ahmed was born in Nottingham on 13 August 2004. He came through the youth system at Nottinghamshire before moving to Leicestershire in 2017.

He was spotted early. At 13 he was already talked about as one of the most exciting young players in the country, and he was asked to bowl to the England and West Indies squads at Lord's. One of his deliveries hit Ben Stokes's stumps, which is a fine thing to tell people at school the next morning.

The player

He is a right-arm leg-spinner with a googly in his armoury, and the steadiness of his bowling has won him praise. His List A debut for Leicestershire came in July 2021, and early in 2022 he went to the West Indies with England's side for the Under-19 World Cup, taking 12 wickets in four games as they reached the final. A first-class debut followed in May 2022.

By December of that year he was in Pakistan with the Test squad, and on 17 December 2022 he became England's youngest Test cricketer, aged 18 years and 126 days. In Pakistan's second innings he took 5 for 48, and no younger man had ever taken five wickets on his Test debut. In 2024, in India, he took 11 wickets in three Tests. Across his 5 Tests between 2022 and 2024 he took 22 wickets at 31.23 and made 103 runs.

What made him special

Leg-spin is a tricky art, and England trusted him with it in a Test match at 18. He also kept breaking age records. In March 2023 he became the youngest man to win caps for England in all three international formats, after first appearances in one-day and T20 cricket against Bangladesh.

His batting in Tests was a work in progress, with a top score of 28, but he could hit hard when the moment called for it. At the T20 World Cup in February 2026, in a Super 8 game against New Zealand, he took 2 for 28 and then struck 19 not out from seven balls to win the match and top the group.

Away from the middle

The Southern Brave signed him for The Hundred in 2022. He was shortlisted for the BBC Young Sports Personality of the Year in 2022, and in 2025 the Professional Cricketers' Association named him its Men's Young Player of the Year.

And finally

Plenty of cricketers wait years for a Test cap. He had one at 18, a five-wicket haul on the third day of it, and caps in all three formats before his 19th birthday. Most of us were a long way from landing a googly at that age.
